title: U.S. Energy Storage Market Posts Record 18.9 GWh in Q2 as Longer-Duration Systems Drive Growth
gist: The U.S. installed a record 18.9 GWh (5.4 GW) of battery energy storage in Q2 2026 — GWh up 17% YoY even as GW capacity fell 7% — as average system duration jumped from 2.8 to 3.5 hours, driven by resource-adequacy needs, California long-duration projects and Texas utility-contracted assets. ACP/Wood Mackenzie's Energy Storage Monitor forecasts the market to more than 50% MW growth over five years to 207 GW/715 GWh cumulative by 2031, propelled by data-center-driven utility-scale demand even as residential storage contracts in 2026 on tax-credit elimination and near-term trade-driven supply bottlenecks delay utility-scale growth until 2028.

insights.claim: The U.S. installed a record 5.4 GW / 18.9 GWh of battery energy storage systems in Q2 2026, with total GW installations down 7% year-over-year but GWh up 17% year-over-year, marking a new energy (GWh) record for the market.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The divergence between falling MW and rising GWh installations signals the market's real growth vector has shifted to duration/energy capacity, not just power capacity — a key input for sizing storage-component and cell demand.
insights.quote: The U.S. installed 5.4 GW/18.9 GWh of battery energy storage systems in Q2 2026.

insights.claim: The national average duration of installed U.S. battery energy storage systems increased from 2.8 hours to 3.5 hours year-over-year, driven by resource adequacy needs.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 25% jump in average system duration in one year signals utilities and developers are shifting procurement toward longer-duration systems to meet capacity/resource-adequacy requirements — favorable for LFP and longer-duration chemistry suppliers.
insights.quote: The national average duration of installed battery energy storage systems increased from 2.8 hours to 3.5 hours, driven by resource adequacy needs.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie and the American Clean Power Association forecast annual U.S. energy storage installations to grow over 50% in MW terms over the next five years, reaching 207 GW and 715 GWh installed cumulatively by 2031.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 207 GW/715 GWh cumulative 2031 target is the benchmark investors should use to size the multi-year addressable market for battery cells, EPC, and grid-storage financing in the U.S.
insights.quote: Annual US energy storage installations to grow over 50% in MW terms over the next five years, reaching 207 GW/715 GWh installed cumulatively by 2031.

insights.claim: Utility-scale storage deployments totaled 4.7 GW/17.6 GWh in Q2 2026, down 8% year-over-year in MW terms as key state markets become increasingly saturated.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Saturation in established utility-scale markets (e.g., California, Texas) means incremental growth must increasingly come from newer state markets — watch for pipeline shifts to secondary markets.
insights.quote: Utility-scale deployments totaled 4.7 GW/17.6 GWh in Q2, down 8% y-o-y in MW terms as key markets become increasingly saturated.

insights.claim: Despite the Q2 MW decline, first-half-2026 utility-scale installations were up 5% year-over-year, signaling that full-year 2026 installations will likely land on par with 2025.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The H1 2026 data implies quarterly volatility (Q2 dip) shouldn't be read as an annual trend break — full-year utility-scale volumes are tracking flat versus 2025, not declining.
insights.quote: However, in the first half of 2026, installations were up 5% y-o-y, signaling that 2026 installations will remain on par with last year.

insights.claim: Average utility-scale project duration continued climbing in Q2 2026, driven in part by a long-duration storage project in California built to meet state targets, and utility-contracted storage assets deployed in Texas.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: California and Texas are the specific states driving the national duration shift — useful for state-level project pipeline tracking and policy-driven demand forecasting.
insights.quote: Average project duration continued to climb in Q2 2026, driven in part by a long-duration project in California designed to meet state targets and utility-contracted storage assets deployed in Texas.

insights.claim: The share of hybrid (co-located solar/storage) utility-scale installations shrank to 33% in Q2 2026, down from 45% in Q2 2025, due to a contraction in the California market.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 12-point drop in hybrid installation share indicates standalone storage is gaining relative share of new utility-scale builds as California's hybrid-heavy pipeline cools — relevant to interconnection-queue and tax-credit-structuring strategy.
insights.quote: The share of hybrid utility-scale installations shrank to 33% in Q2 2026, down from 45% in Q2 2025, due to a contraction in the California market.

insights.claim: Utility-scale battery system prices fell 2% year-over-year to $916/kW in Q2 2026, continuing a downward cost trend that is helping storage compete across more regions and use cases.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A concrete $916/kW benchmark for utility-scale battery systems anchors cost-competitiveness modeling versus gas peakers and informs procurement/pricing negotiations.
insights.quote: Utility-scale battery system prices fell 2% year-over-year to $916/kW in Q2 2026, continuing a downward cost trend that is helping storage compete across more regions and use cases.

insights.claim: The residential storage sector installed 676 MW in Q2 2026 — its fourth largest quarter on record — representing a 15% quarter-over-quarter decline but a 3% year-over-year increase.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Despite a strong Q2 by historical standards, the sequential 15% QoQ drop flags a decelerating near-term trend worth monitoring against the full-year contraction forecast.
insights.quote: The residential sector recorded its fourth largest quarter on record in Q2 2026, installing 676 MW, a 15% quarter-over-quarter (q-o-q) decline, and 3% y-o-y increase.

insights.claim: The national residential storage market is expected to contract 4% in 2026, driven by tax credit elimination, consumer hesitancy, and a challenging transition away from third-party-ownership financing models.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A named policy driver (tax credit elimination) plus a financing-model transition risk gives investors two concrete catalysts to monitor for residential storage demand deterioration in 2026.
insights.quote: Overall, the national residential storage market is expected to contract by 4% in 2026 amid tax credit elimination, consumer hesitancy, and a challenging third-party-ownership transition.

insights.claim: The top five U.S. residential storage markets — California, Texas, Puerto Rico, Arizona and Illinois — accounted for 88% of residential storage capacity installed in Q2 2026, though all five declined quarter-over-quarter.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: 88% concentration in five states means residential storage revenue is highly exposed to policy/rate changes in just those markets; a synchronized QoQ decline across all five signals a broad-based, not state-specific, slowdown.
insights.quote: The top five U.S. markets, California, Texas, Puerto Rico, Arizona and Illinois, accounted for 88% of residential storage capacity installed in Q2, though all five declined q-o-q.

insights.claim: Puerto Rico's residential storage market contracted the most in absolute terms among top markets, falling from 129 MW in Q1 2026 to 73 MW in Q2 2026.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 43% sequential drop in Puerto Rico residential storage is a specific market to investigate for policy, grid, or financing disruptions given its outsized prior contribution.
insights.quote: Puerto Rico contracted the most in absolute terms, falling from 129 MW in Q1 to 73 MW in Q2.

insights.claim: The national residential solar-plus-storage attachment rate reached 46% in Q2 2026, up from 41% in Q2 2025, showing continued consumer demand for paired solar-storage systems even as overall residential storage volumes soften.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Rising attachment rate amid falling absolute installs suggests the residential storage decline is driven by fewer new solar installs overall, not by weakening storage attach economics — an important distinction for solar-attached storage suppliers.
insights.quote: The national residential solar-plus-storage attachment rate reached 46% in Q2 2026, up from 41% in Q2 2025, reflecting continued consumer demand for paired solar and storage installations despite broader residential market headwinds.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie forecasts the residential storage market to rebound between 2027 and 2031, growing at an average annual rate of 9% after the 2026 contraction.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The forecast implies 2026 is viewed as a trough year for residential storage, with a multi-year rebound expected from 2027 — relevant for timing residential-storage-exposed equity and financing entries.
insights.quote: The residential market is expected to rebound between 2027 and 2031, growing at an average annual rate of 9%.

insights.claim: The Community, Commercial and Industrial (CCI) storage sector installed 48 MW in Q2 2026, returning to historical deployment levels after California's record Q1 2026 driven by the state's Net Energy Metering 2.0 grandfathering deadline.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The Q1 spike and Q2 reversion confirms NEM 2.0 grandfathering was a one-time pull-forward of California CCI demand, not a sustained step-change — don't extrapolate Q1 run-rates.
insights.quote: The Community, Commercial and Industrial (CCI) sector installed 48 MW, returning to historical deployment levels after California's record Q1 driven by the state’s Net Energy Metering 2.0 grandfathering deadline.

insights.claim: The CCI sector saw an overall 2% year-over-year decline in Q2 2026, but above-average growth in Hawaii, New Mexico and Texas partially offset the contraction.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Emerging CCI growth markets (Hawaii, New Mexico, Texas) are diversifying the segment beyond California dependence, offering new geographic exposure for CCI storage developers.
insights.quote: Overall, the market saw a slight decline of 2% year-over-year, but above average growth in Hawaii, New Mexico and Texas helped offset some of this contraction.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie projects the CCI storage sector to grow 27% annually between 2026 and 2031 as deployment expands beyond California into emerging markets such as Maryland and Texas.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: 27% projected CCI growth, with explicit geographic expansion beyond California named (Maryland, Texas), flags where CCI storage developers should be building pipeline next.
insights.quote: The CCI sector is projected to grow 27% between 2026 and 2031 as deployment expands beyond California into emerging markets such as Maryland and Texas.

themes.theme: Data centers as a structural demand driver

insights.claim: Rising data center electricity demand is expected to drive utility-scale storage to 8% average annual growth over the next five years, as storage becomes a faster, cheaper, and more reliable capacity solution than gas alone amid hyperscaler grid-connection bottlenecks.
insights.speaker: Allison Feeney
insights.so_what: Storage is being positioned as a direct substitute/complement to gas peakers for data-center speed-to-power, a structural tailwind for utility-scale battery capex tied to the AI/data-center buildout.
insights.quote: Data center buildout strengthens the U.S. storage outlook across all sectors. Storage can provide needed capacity faster, cheaper and more reliably than gas alone.
insights.locator: quote from Allison Feeney, Wood Mackenzie research analyst

insights.claim: As hyperscalers increasingly face grid-connection bottlenecks, utility-scale storage is positioned to enable faster 'speed to power' for new data center capacity.
insights.speaker: Allison Feeney
insights.so_what: Grid-interconnection-constrained hyperscalers create a direct commercial use case for utility-scale storage as an interconnection workaround — a monetizable niche for storage developers targeting data center campuses.
insights.quote: As hyperscalers increasingly face grid-connection bottlenecks, utility-scale storage will enable speed to power for data centers.
insights.locator: quote from Allison Feeney, Wood Mackenzie research analyst

insights.claim: The industry is increasingly positioning virtual power plants (VPPs) as a key enabler of load growth, broadening distributed storage's value proposition beyond customer-centric benefits and unlocking new participation pathways for both the CCI and residential segments.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: VPP monetization is emerging as a second revenue stream layered on top of behind-the-meter storage, relevant to distributed-storage software/aggregator business models.
insights.quote: The industry is increasingly positioning virtual power plants (VPPs) as a key enabler of load growth, unlocking new participation pathways for the CCI and residential segments alike.

themes.theme: Supply chain, trade policy and manufacturing shift

insights.claim: Potential trade restrictions and other supply chain dynamics could cause near-term bottlenecks, and the utility-scale storage segment may see stagnation in 2026 and 2027 as the industry adapts.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Trade-policy-driven bottlenecks are flagged as a near-term (2026-2027) growth-stagnation risk for utility-scale storage, separate from and additional to market saturation — a risk factor to price into near-term capex plans.
insights.quote: Supply chain dynamics, including potential trade restrictions, could cause near-term bottlenecks. The utility-scale segment may see some stagnation in 2026 and 2027 as the industry adapts.

insights.claim: Utility-scale storage growth is forecast to resume in 2028 and scale at 11% average annual growth through 2031 as domestic battery cell manufacturing capacity ramps up.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: 2028 is flagged as the inflection point when domestic cell manufacturing capacity is expected to resolve current supply bottlenecks — a timing marker for battery manufacturing capex and localization plays.
insights.quote: However, growth is forecast to resume in 2028, scaling at 11% on average annually through 2031 as domestic cell manufacturing ramps up.

insights.claim: Slowing EV demand has become an unexpected tailwind for stationary storage, as manufacturers repurpose idle EV battery cell capacity to accelerate the domestic storage supply base just as trade policy makes domestic sourcing more valuable.
insights.speaker: Allison Weis
insights.so_what: A structural cross-subsidy is emerging: weak EV demand is freeing up battery cell capacity for grid storage, potentially accelerating domestic storage supply chains faster than standalone storage-driven capex would — relevant for battery manufacturer diversification strategy and trade-policy arbitrage.
insights.quote: The slowdown in EV demand has become an unexpected tailwind for storage. Manufacturers are repurposing idle EV cell capacity, accelerating the domestic supply base just as trade policy makes it most valuable.
insights.locator: quote from Allison Weis, Global Head of Energy Storage, Wood Mackenzie

insights.claim: American Clean Power's John Hensley characterizes battery storage as one of the most important tools to meet growing U.S. electricity demand, citing its ability to deploy quickly, strengthen reliability, and better utilize existing and new generation, with a strong pipeline supporting an exceptionally strong outlook.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Industry-association-level conviction (ACP) that storage's outlook is 'exceptionally strong' reinforces the bull case underpinning the 207 GW/715 GWh 2031 forecast.
insights.quote: Battery storage is one of the most important tools we have to meet growing electricity demand. Storage can be deployed quickly, strengthens reliability, and helps the grid make better use of both existing and new generation. With a strong pipeline and continued technology improvements, the outlook for storage remains exceptionally strong.
insights.locator: quote from John Hensley, ACP Senior Vice President of Markets and Policy Analysis
